audit_items.proof_trace: The property requires that no log entry contain auth_code[0:20], but L34 unconditionally executes `console.log('[AUTH CALLBACK] Code (first 20 chars):', code.substring(0, 20) + '...')` inside the `if (code)` branch with no environment guard or redaction. The Phase 02c note claiming the code is only logged as a boolean was incorrect — the actual code logs the 20-char prefix on every OAuth callback invocation.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Any party with read access to server-side logs (container stdout, log aggregation service, or host-level log files) can extract the first 20 characters of a live OAuth authorization code during the brief window before it is exchanged, enabling a replay attack or session hijack if the code has sufficient entropy leakage.
